chapter: Bix, Trumbauer and the Goldkette sidemen
title: Trumbauer sessions without Morehouse: Harold McDonald and Harry Gale
summary: Kline asks why other drummers like Harold McDonald and Harry Gale appeared on Trumbauer records, and Morehouse cannot say.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Okay, now I understand, sure. Okay, let me move on. There were several records that Frankie Trumbauer while you were still with Jean Goldkette.
Yes.
Frankie Trumbauer was making some records. with you and Jimmy Dorsey, Doc Ryker, Paul Mertz, Eddie Lang.
It sounds like the Jean Goldkette orchestra but they are under the Frankie Trumbauer and his orchestra label.
That's right.
Then you made - they made a couple of records in 1927, getting on, that you were replaced by a man named Harold McDonald.
Yeah.
And I wonder who was Harold McDonald and why weren't you on the record? Do you remember? Where did he come from? Why didn't you make it?
Well Harold McDonald was down here...
What was the name of the record?
The record - okay, the record was 'Sugar' - no. The record was... 'From Monday On', 'Mississippi Mud'.
Harold McDonald darling, from Monday On. Do you remember 'Mississippi Mud'.
You weren't on 'Mississippi Mud'.
Yes, I was.
You were.
How come... No, this is what...
Okay, right. This is hard to remember, all these things, right. Okay I don't know what happened to Harold McDonald but we don't hear from him again.
No.
Okay. Then Harry Gale.
Harry Gale?
Played the drums with Frankie Trumbauer. You don't remember him.
No.
